messages.subject: units
parts:
Please pardon this novice question. I'm new to the Distance software.

I've run analyses on data collected from a shipboard visual survey (line transect).
As expected, Distance complains about too few data points.
Data was entered with units of
Region: square kilometers
Line length: kilometers
Distance from line: kilometers

I've searched the User Guide several times, but can't find the units used for the density estimates in Results.
The Results page for Estimation Summary - Density & Abundance reports

                         Estimate      %CV     df     95% Confidence Interval
                        ------------------------------------------------------
 Half-normal/Cosine     
                 DS      1.1461       38.06    28.67 0.53999       2.4324    
                 D       31.985       47.08    54.58  13.044       78.428    
                 N      0.53591E+07   47.08    54.58 0.21856E+07  0.13141E+08

I've found reference that D=Density and N=Expected Number in Specified Area, but I'm not sure of the units for density or what is the Specified Area.

Can you lead me to more detailed explanation of how to interpret the Results?

thank you,
Woody Sutherland
UC San Diego

Woody:

Have a look in your results but not on the summary page.  Instead, look on page(s) that look like this:

Stratum       : xxxxx
Effort        :    856.1700   
# samples     :    20
Width         :    1000.000   
Left          :       0.0000000
# observations:    34

 Model
    Hazard Rate key, k(y) = 1 - Exp(-(y/A(1))**-A(2))
    Cosine adjustments of order(s) :  2


              Point        Standard    Percent Coef.        95% Percent
  Parameter   Estimate       Error      of Variation     Confidence Interval
  ---------  -----------  -----------  --------------  ----------------------
    DS       0.55749E-01  0.14195E-01      25.46      0.33466E-01  0.92869E-01
    E(S)      1.1992      0.81707E-01       6.81       1.0440       1.3775   
    D        0.66855E-01  0.17621E-01      26.36      0.39542E-01  0.11303   
    N         69.000       18.187          26.36       41.000       117.00   
  ---------  -----------  -----------  --------------  ----------------------

 Measurement Units               
 ---------------------------------
 Density: Numbers/Sq. kilometers
     ESW: meters        

 Component Percentages of Var(D)
 -------------------------------
 Detection probability   :  22.2
 Encounter rate          :  71.2
 Cluster size            :   6.7

You see spelled out below the table of estimates, the units in which the estimates are expressed.  This information is also available to you by looking in the Log window where all the options you provided for your analysis are echoed:

 Options;                                                                     
 Type=Line;                                                                   
 Length /Measure='Kilometer';                                                 
 Distance=Perp /Measure='Meter';                                              
 Area /Units='Square kilometer';      <<<======                                        
 Object=Cluster;                                                              
 SF=1;                                                                        
 Selection=Sequential;                                                        
 Lookahead=1;                                                                 
 Maxterms=5;                                                                  
 Confidence=95;                                                               
 Print=Selection;                                                             
 End; 

From the information you provided, your density estimates are expressed in numbers per square kilometer.  The abundance is the density (per unit area) multiplied by the size of your study area (you specified this when you specified the size of your study area, or size of your strata).  Working backward from the information you provided, I believe your study area was 167550 km^2 (which is the ratio of estimated abundance and estimated density (per km^2).

Any other questions, just ask.
